overall_summary: Weak jobs data is driving fresh dovish Fed bets that should support risk assets. Bitcoin has already cleared 61k and ETF inflows remain strong. Geopolitical noise adds little immediate directional pressure with markets closed.
key_points: Bitcoin surges past 61k on weak jobs data
Spot ETFs see 223 million dollar inflows
Dovish Fed odds rise after soft payrolls
US markets shut for July 4 holiday
Geopolitical headlines stay unresolved and neutral

items.title: Bitcoin Surges Above $61,000 on Weak US Jobs Data
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed over 4 percent to top $61,000 on Thursday after the June jobs report showed only 57,000 new positions added, well below the expected 115,000. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh comments that inflation risks have eased added to the dovish tone, cutting odds of a July rate hike. Traders should care because softer macro data often supports risk assets like Bitcoin in the near term.
items.impact: Positive short-term momentum for BTC and risk assets.

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Post $223 Million Net Inflow on July 2
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a daily net inflow of about $223.5 million on July 2 according to tracking data. This reverses a recent streak of outflows and coincided with the price rally. Traders should watch because sustained inflows signal renewed institutional demand that can support higher prices.
items.impact: Supports upward price pressure through increased buying.

items.title: Weak June Jobs Report Sparks Dovish Fed Bets
items.summary: US employers added just 57,000 jobs in June, well below expectations, with prior months revised lower. The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.2 percent, but labor force participation hit a multi-year low outside the pandemic. Markets are now pricing lower odds of near-term Fed rate hikes, sending the dollar lower and Treasury yields down while stocks rose. Crypto traders should watch this closely because softer labor data tilts policy expectations toward easier financial conditions that have historically supported risk assets.
items.impact: Reduces near-term rate-hike odds, supporting risk assets like Bitcoin via potential liquidity tailwinds.

items.title: US Markets Closed for July 4 Holiday
items.summary: No major US economic data releases are scheduled today as markets observe Independence Day. Trading desks are digesting yesterday's jobs report instead, with limited fresh macro catalysts expected until next week. Crypto traders can use the quiet session to position ahead of potential weekend flows or Monday's reopening.
items.impact: Low volatility day with focus remaining on jobs-report implications rather than new data.

items.title: Iran Begins Massive Funeral for Slain Leader Khamenei
items.summary: Ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, killed in February US-Israeli strikes, start today in Tehran with processions across multiple cities and burial set for July 9 in Mashhad. Millions of mourners are expected amid tight security. Traders should watch for any signs of unrest or regime messaging that could reignite Middle East tensions and oil supply worries.
items.impact: May add to regional uncertainty and support oil prices on risk premium.

items.title: UN Security Council Holds Emergency Meeting on Iran Attacks
items.summary: The UNSC met urgently on July 2 over recent Iranian strikes in Bahrain and Kuwait plus ongoing Gulf tensions around the Strait of Hormuz. Iran and the US continue trading accusations while a fragile ceasefire holds. Traders should monitor any resolution or escalation signals that could disrupt energy flows.
items.impact: Sustains geopolitical risk premium in oil and risk assets until resolved.

items.title: Iran Military Chief Vows Revenge Amid Khamenei Mourning
items.summary: Iran's top military official pledged to avenge the slain supreme leader as funeral events begin. Combined with fresh warnings on Hormuz transit, this keeps tensions simmering despite ceasefire talks. Crypto and equity traders should note the potential for sudden volatility in risk sentiment.
items.impact: Maintains elevated oil and risk-off pressure until de-escalation confirms.

items.title: Russian Strikes Kill Dozens in Kyiv and Other Ukrainian Cities
items.summary: Overnight Russian missile and drone attacks killed at least 30 in Kyiv and others elsewhere, with rescuers clearing rubble. The war continues with no immediate end in sight. Traders watch energy and grain markets plus broader risk appetite for spillover effects.
items.impact: Adds to European energy and global risk uncertainty.

items.title: US-Iran Ceasefire Talks Show Mixed Signals on Hormuz
items.summary: Progress reported in some US-Iran channels while Iran issues warnings on approved shipping routes through the Strait. The situation remains fragile with potential for quick reversals. Markets price in ongoing energy chokepoint risk.
items.impact: Keeps oil volatility elevated; resolution would ease pressure.

items.title: US Withdraws Forces from Nigeria After ISIS Operation
items.summary: AFRICOM confirms US troops pulled out following a targeted operation against ISIS in Nigeria. Limited immediate global market impact but part of shifting US posture in Africa. Watch for any secondary effects on regional stability narratives.
items.impact: Minor, localized risk reduction with little broad asset impact.
